limitations.text:
Limitations — Familial-Risk Synthetic Patient Profile
Clinical Data (Synthea)
Family history relationships/conditions confirmed via SNOMED coding, not free text — same coding-reliability caveats noted for the companion Stage 3 profile apply generally to this Synthea build
Single simulated life path — no alternative outcome (e.g., subject developing the same familial disease) represented
Light record (179 total FHIR entries) limits longitudinal vital-sign trend analysis compared to the companion profile
Wearable Donor Selection (LifeSnaps)
Race not matchable — attribute absent from source dataset
Age matchable only at a coarse threshold (<30 / ≥30), not exact age
Selection ranked by BMI proximity and data completeness, not a validated “healthy young adult” profile standard
Two closer BMI matches were excluded solely for missing HRV data — selection is data-availability-constrained, not purely criteria-optimal
Unmeasured confounders in the donor’s original recording period inherited without detection
Wearable Data Treatment
No modification applied — assumes the donor’s real baseline is an adequate stand-in for this subject’s true physiology, which is unverified
No representation of subclinical risk (e.g., mild insulin resistance, early vascular changes) that could plausibly be present given family history, despite normal lab/vital values on record
Data Integration
Clinical–wearable correspondence is constructed (sex-matched, BMI-proximity-ranked), not a unified measurement process
No downstream validation against clinical judgment or an established risk-stratification method
No connection established between this profile and the companion Stage 3 profile beyond shared disease-pathway framing — not a true genetic or simulation-level link

methodology.text:
A Synthetic Multi-Modal Patient Profile for Familial CKD Risk Without Active Disease: Clinical and Wearable Data Integration
Subject: Vernon254 Alfonzo975 Wunsch504 (synthetic)
1. Clinical Data Generation
1.1 Population synthesis and candidate identification
The subject was drawn from the same Synthea-generated Massachusetts population used for the companion Stage 3 CKD profile. Candidate identification for this profile targeted patients with documented FamilyMemberHistory records indicating renal or metabolic disease in first-degree relatives, combined with an absence of any active personal Condition matching the same disease category — intended to represent a genetically/familially at-risk but currently asymptomatic subject.
1.2 Subject validation
The selected subject’s record was confirmed against the following criteria:
No active Condition entries indicating diabetes, hypertension, or renal disease — the personal condition list contains only resolved acute or situational entries (viral pharyngitis, stress, gingivitis)
FamilyMemberHistory records documenting Type 2 diabetes, essential hypertension, and CKD (Stage 2 and Stage 3, with end-stage renal disease in one relative) across father, mother, and brother
Baseline vitals consistent with early cardiometabolic risk rather than disease: BMI 28.07 (overweight, sub-obese threshold), blood pressure 127/73 (high-normal, sub-hypertensive), no active pharmacological treatment
This profile is intended to complement the Stage 3 CKD subject as a paired presymptomatic comparator sharing the same underlying disease pathway.
2. Wearable Data Source Selection
2.1 Target demographic profile
Male, date of birth 1996-12-24 (age 29 at time of wearable data collection), White.
2.2 Donor pool constraints
As with the companion profile, LifeSnaps records only gender and a binary age indicator (<30 / ≥30), with no race or ethnicity field. Filtering to male participants aged <30 yielded 21 candidates, all demographically equivalent beyond this threshold.
2.3 Selection procedure
Selection criteria were inverted relative to the companion Stage 3 profile: rather than ranking for cardiometabolic risk indicators, candidates were ranked for proximity to the subject’s actual recorded BMI (28.07) among those with complete heart rate variability (RMSSD) data. Two candidates matched BMI more closely (28.0) but lacked RMSSD entirely; the selected candidate (BMI 29.0, resting heart rate 61.7 bpm, RMSSD 72.8 ms) was chosen for the combination of close BMI match, physiologically normal resting heart rate, and the largest available longitudinal depth among all candidates (223 days).
3. Wearable Data Treatment
No disease-state physiological modification was applied to this subject’s wearable data. Because the subject carries no active diagnosed condition, the donor’s recorded values were used as-is, representing an unmodified healthy baseline rather than a disease-adjusted signature. This is a deliberate contrast with the companion Stage 3 CKD profile, where modifications were calibrated to a diagnosed and clinically established disease state.
4. Temporal Alignment
The wearable dataset’s native collection window (2021-06-14 to 2022-01-22) was shifted forward by a constant offset to terminate at the present date, consistent with the temporal alignment method applied to the companion profile. The resulting window spans 2026-01-26 to 2026-09-05, preserving the original 223-day relative structure.

family_history_no_conditions_Vernon254_Wunsch504.json — clinical record (FHIR)
